To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we proposed a novel deep learning model based on recurrent- convolutional neural networks (RCNNS) that can automatically learn useful representations for schizophrenia diagnosis from 4-D f-MRI recordings; 2) we evaluated our RCNNs on a publicly available dataset and compared them with other state-of-the-art machine learning models.

(a) the proposed recurrent-convolution neural network (R-CNN) model outperforms the traditional machine learning methods in terms of classification accuracy and (b) the proposed R-CNN model is capable of learning the spatial and temporal information of the brain functional connectivity in an unsupervised manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Can a recurrent neural network learn to extract useful features for the diagnosis of patients with schizophrenia from functional MRI movies?
the following two questions: (1) What is the most suitable way to represent fMRI recordings in order to capture both the spatial and the temporal information in the data?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed method outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness.
we developed a novel approach to automatically learn useful features from 4-D fMRIs for schizophrenia classification.
the proposed method can learn the neural markers of the schizophrenia disorder and can achieve a high classification accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method is able to learn the most discriminative representations of the brain functional imaging data for identifying schizophrenia patients.
we are able to learn neural markers of schizophrenia disorder using recurrent neural networks, and the learned markers are more robust than the conventional ones.
we propose a new deep learning framework that can automatically learn useful representations of the functional MRI data and use them for classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a deep learning method can learn useful information for the task of classifying patients with schizophrenia from functional MRI data.
a recurrent-convolution neural network can be used to learn useful representations from functional MRI movies and that the resulting representations can be used to identify schizophrenia patients.
the recurrent-convolution neural network (RCNN) architecture can automatically learn useful representations directly from the fMRI movie.
